append.text: **Ps 120:3–4 *neque dormítet … non dormitábit neque dórmiet* → *nem dormite … não dormitará nem dormirá*** — the row's own reason (the pair νυστάζω / ὑπνόω, doze / sleep). The ambiguity reader listed *dormite* and *dormitará* as unknown (the third and fourth blind readers to do so) and heard the pair as a mere repetition. **Proposed (open), for the main session: *cochilar*** — the plain Brazilian word for exactly this (DM1962 *Não, não cochila, nem dorme*; the CNBB Liturgia das Horas *ele não dorme nem cochila*, verified, `consult/web-lh-salmo-120-121.md`); it would make the two degrees audible. Cost: homely register; 118:28 and 75:7 would follow. Option in Ps 120's decision `dormitare`.

**Ps 120:6 *Per diem sol non uret te: neque luna per noctem* → *De dia o sol não te queimará: nem a lua de noite*** — the row's option taken for length (with *Durante o dia … durante a noite* the colons were +5 and +3 on the Latin's 8 and 7); DM1962's pair; passed the Latinist twice; the stylist's best line. *Durante* the option.
Ps 120:8 *ex hoc nunc, et usque in sǽculum* → *desde agora e para todo o sempre* (= 112:2b, 113:26).
Ps 120:2 *O meu auxílio vem do Senhor, * que fez o céu e a terra* — the formula as it stands, the relative right after *Senhor*; the Monday Vespers antiphon of the older psalter.

**Ps 120:3 *Non det in commotiónem pedem tuum* → *Que não deixe vacilar o teu pé*** — the jussive with *Que*: bare *Não deixe vacilar* is heard in Brazil as a command to the listener (*deixe* the everyday imperative). Draft 1 *Que ele não deixe* (the stylist: hiatus, written grammar).
Ps 120:1 *Levávi óculos meos in montes* → *Levantei os meus olhos para os montes*; 122:1 *Ad te levávi óculos meos* should follow.

**auxílium → auxílio too** (Ps 120:1–2, the word picked up from verse to verse; 59:13). The CNBB Liturgia das Horas, MS1932 and DM1962 have *socorro* in Ps 120 (verified) — *socorro* is ops's (D41); option in Ps 120.

Ps 120:5 *super manum déxteram tuam* → *sobre a tua mão direita* (the hand named; *super* kept against the Hebrew's 'at'); the ambiguity reader was unsure why the hand; *à tua mão direita* the option.

terms: | úrere | queimar (*De dia o sol não te queimará*) | working | Ps 120:6 (συγκαύσει); = 25:2 *ure renes meos* → *queimai*. |
